title: Stalinist show trials target Hungarian Catholic Church leadership
note: Mindszenty imprisoned 1949; mass persecution of Church in 1950 confirmed.

title: Hungary completes nationalization of remaining private industry
note: Nationalization of small enterprises completed ~1950 under Rákosi confirmed.

title: ÁVH secret police reaches peak power with mass surveillance network
note: ÁVH under Gábor Péter, ~28,000 agents, pervasive terror confirmed.

title: Stalin's death triggers political thaw; Imre Nagy appointed Prime Minister
note: Stalin died March 1953; Nagy appointed PM, New Course policy confirmed.

title: Hungary's Golden Team reaches 1954 FIFA World Cup final
note: Hungary lost 3–2 to West Germany (Miracle of Bern); beat WG 8–3 in group stage confirmed.

title: Hungary joins the Warsaw Pact as a founding member
note: Hungary was founding signatory of Warsaw Pact, May 14, 1955, confirmed.

title: Khrushchev's Secret Speech and Rákosi's fall ignite reform expectations
note: Secret Speech Feb 1956; Rákosi replaced by Gerő July 1956; Petőfi Circle confirmed.

title: Hungarian Revolution begins October 23 with mass protests in Budapest
note: October 23 student uprising, Stalin statue toppled, Nagy recalled as PM confirmed.

title: Soviet tanks crush the Hungarian Revolution on November 4
note: Operation Whirlwind Nov 4; ~2,500 Hungarians and ~700 Soviet soldiers killed confirmed.

title: Two hundred thousand Hungarians flee as refugees after the Soviet invasion
note: ~200,000 fled (180,000 to Austria, 20,000 to Yugoslavia) confirmed by UNHCR.

title: Imre Nagy executed after secret trial along with other revolution leaders
note: Nagy, Maléter, Gimes executed June 16, 1958; secret trial; reburied June 16, 1989 confirmed.

title: Kádár announces pragmatic formula: who is not against us is with us
note: Kádár's famous inversion of Stalinist formula and pragmatic social contract confirmed.

title: Agricultural collectivization completed with 95 percent of farmland in cooperatives
note: Second collectivization completed by early 1961 with household plots allowed confirmed.

title: Kádár announces amnesty for most 1956 revolution participants
note: Amnesty decrees 1960–1963 released most 1956 prisoners; 1962 declaration confirmed.

title: Hungarian cultural policy codified as Three Ts: support, toleration, prohibition
note: Three Ts (támogatás, tűrés, tiltás) framework confirmed as Kádár-era cultural policy.

title: Vatican-Hungary agreement restores partial Catholic Church appointments
note: 1964 Vatican-Hungary partial accord on bishop appointments (Ostpolitik) confirmed.

title: Preparation of New Economic Mechanism begins under reform economists
note: May 7, 1966 Central Committee announcement; Rezső Nyers led reform team confirmed.

title: New Economic Mechanism launched, introducing market elements into Hungarian socialism
note: NEM launched January 1, 1968; abolished mandatory quotas; market price signals confirmed.

title: Hungary participates in Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia
note: Hungarian troops participated in August 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia confirmed.

title: Hardline Communist Party faction rolls back NEM economic reforms
note: Conservative rollback of NEM in 1972; Nyers removed from senior positions confirmed.

title: Oil shock exposes Hungary's energy dependence on Soviet and global supplies
note: 1973 oil shock and gradual Soviet shift to world-market pricing impacted Hungary confirmed.

title: Hungary builds extensive Western debt to sustain consumption and investment
note: Large-scale Western borrowing mid-1970s to finance consumption and investment confirmed.

title: Hungary signs Helsinki Accords, accepting human rights commitments
note: Hungary signed Helsinki Final Act 1975; human rights basket used by dissidents confirmed.

title: Dissident intellectual circles form democratic opposition movement in Budapest
note: Konrád, Szelényi and samizdat circles in Budapest ~1976–77 confirmed; categorized as mass_protest is weak but facts correct.

title: United States returns the Hungarian Holy Crown, improving bilateral relations
note: Crown returned January 6, 1978 by Sec. of State Vance on Carter's order confirmed.

title: Rubik's Cube licensed for international production, becoming a global phenomenon
note: International deal signed Sept 1979 with Ideal Toys; Rubik invented it 1974 confirmed. 350M vs 500M figure is minor—event facts correct.

title: Hungary applies for IMF and World Bank membership to address debt crisis
note: World Bank application filed November 4, 1981; IMF application same period confirmed.

title: Hungary becomes first Warsaw Pact country to join the IMF and World Bank
note: Romania joined IMF December 1972, making it the first Warsaw Pact/COMECON country. Hungary was the SECOND Soviet-bloc nation. The 'first Warsaw Pact country' claim is materially wrong.

title: Enterprise law allows formation of small private companies alongside state sector
note: 1983 enterprise law permitting small private companies confirmed.

title: Opposition activists hold landmark independent political gathering at Monor
note: Monor meeting June 1985, ~45 intellectuals, samizdat circulation confirmed.

title: Chernobyl disaster raises nuclear safety concerns about Hungary's Paks plant
note: Chernobyl April 1986; Paks uses Soviet VVER reactors; environmental movement boosted confirmed.

title: Lakitelek meeting founds Hungarian Democratic Forum as first independent party
note: MDF founded at Lakitelek September 27, 1987 confirmed.

title: FIDESZ liberal anti-communist youth organization founded by law students
note: FIDESZ was founded March 30, 1988 — not 1987. Year is off by 1. Founding details otherwise accurate.

title: Mass protest against Bős-Nagymaros dam becomes landmark civil society event
note: Dam protests 1988 including ~30,000 in September; landmark civil society event confirmed. 'Tens of thousands' supported by evidence.

title: Kádár removed from power after 32 years; reform communist Grósz takes over
note: Kádár removed May 22, 1988; Grósz became General Secretary confirmed.

title: Imre Nagy reburied in state ceremony; Hungary opens border with Austria
note: Nagy reburied June 16, 1989; Orbán's speech; border opened May 1989; East Germans Sept 1989 confirmed.

title: National Roundtable negotiations produce peaceful democratic transition framework
note: National Roundtable June–September 1989; multiparty framework confirmed.

title: Hungary holds first free multiparty elections since 1947; MDF forms government
note: Elections March–April 1990; MDF won 24.7%; Antall as PM confirmed. 'Since 1947' accurate.

title: Soviet troops begin withdrawal from Hungary after 47 years of occupation
note: Withdrawal began 1990; last Soviet soldier left June 19, 1991 confirmed.

title: Economic transition shock produces sharp GDP decline and mass unemployment
note: ~11% GDP decline 1991; unemployment rose to 10%+ confirmed.

title: Privatization program transfers state enterprises to domestic and foreign buyers
note: State Property Agency privatization; highest FDI per capita in transition economies confirmed.

title: Socialist Party wins landslide; ex-communists return to power democratically
note: MSZP landslide May 1994; peaceful handover; pro-Western reform continued confirmed.

title: Hungary submits formal European Union membership application
note: Hungary applied March 31, 1994 (event says April — off by days only, not a year). Confirmed as among first Central European applicants.

title: Bokros austerity package imposes severe economic stabilization measures
note: Bokros package March 1995; forint devaluation, wage cuts, tuition fees confirmed.

title: NATO invites Hungary to begin accession negotiations at Madrid Summit
note: Madrid Summit July 1997; Hungary, Poland, Czech Republic invited; 85% yes in Nov 1997 referendum confirmed.

title: Viktor Orbán wins elections; FIDESZ forms first government with Orbán as PM
note: Orbán won May 1998 elections; 35-year-old PM; FIDESZ transformed to center-right confirmed.

title: Hungary joins NATO on its 50th anniversary along with Poland and Czech Republic
note: Hungary joined NATO March 12, 1999; 50th anniversary summit in Washington April 1999; Kosovo campaign confirmed.

title: Cyanide spill from Romanian gold mine catastrophically pollutes the Tisza River
note: January 30, 2000 Baia Mare Aurul mine spill; Someș then Tisza contaminated confirmed.

title: Hungarian referendum approves EU membership with 84 percent support
note: April 2003 referendum; 83.8% yes confirmed.

title: Hungary joins the European Union on May 1 in historic enlargement
note: Hungary joined EU May 1, 2004 in 10-country enlargement confirmed.

title: Gyurcsány speech leak triggers riots as PM admits lying to win election
note: Speech leaked September 17, 2006; TV headquarters stormed September 18; 150+ injuries confirmed.

title: Hungary joins the Schengen Area, removing border controls with EU neighbors
note: Hungary joined Schengen December 21, 2007 confirmed.

title: Global financial crisis hits Hungary with exceptional severity requiring IMF bailout
note: October 2008 emergency bailout from IMF/EU/World Bank; Swiss franc mortgage exposure confirmed.

title: FIDESZ wins two-thirds supermajority; Orbán begins constitutional transformation
note: FIDESZ 52.7% vote → two-thirds supermajority; media law, Constitutional Court restructured confirmed.

title: Red sludge disaster in Kolontár kills ten and devastates local communities
note: October 4, 2010; 10 killed, ~150 injured; ~1 million cubic meters released confirmed. Event says '1 million' vs Wikipedia's 1.5 million but order of magnitude correct.

title: Hungary adopts new Fundamental Law replacing 1949 communist-era constitution
note: Fundamental Law adopted April 18, 2011; Venice Commission criticism confirmed.

title: Hungary nationalizes private pension fund assets worth roughly 10 percent of GDP
note: Pension assets nationalized ~$11–12B (event says ~$14B — slightly high but order correct); process was 2010–2011 confirmed.

title: FIDESZ wins third consecutive supermajority; Orbán declares illiberal democracy
note: April 2014 supermajority; July 26, 2014 Tusványos illiberal state speech confirmed. Russia/China/Turkey cited, not 'Russia, China, Turkey' exactly but close.

title: Hungary erects border fence and declares migration crisis emergency
note: Serbian border fence completed September 2015; Dublin suspension; civilizational framing confirmed.

title: Parliament passes law targeting Central European University, effectively expelling it
note: April 2017 law; CEU relocated US-accredited programs to Vienna September 2019 confirmed.

title: European Parliament triggers Article 7 procedure against Hungary over rule-of-law
note: EP voted September 12, 2018; 448 for, 197 against; two-thirds majority confirmed.

title: Emergency powers law grants Orbán indefinite rule by decree during COVID pandemic
note: March 30, 2020 enabling act; indefinite decree powers; 5-year misinformation penalty confirmed.

title: Anti-LGBTQ law prohibits school education on homosexuality and gender issues
note: Passed June 15, 2021; 157–1 vote; von der Leyen 'disgrace' statement confirmed.

title: FIDESZ wins fifth consecutive supermajority despite unified opposition challenge
note: April 2022 election; FIDESZ supermajority against unified opposition confirmed.

title: Russia invades Ukraine; Hungary maintains ambiguous stance breaking with NATO allies
note: February 24, 2022 invasion; Hungary blocked weapons shipments through territory; strained NATO ties confirmed.

title: EU triggers rule-of-law conditionality mechanism, freezing billions in cohesion funds
note: Commission activated April 2022; Council suspended €6.3B cohesion funds December 2022 confirmed. Event says '13.3 billion' — the broader figure is ~€22B total affected; the €6.3B is the formal conditionality-mechanism amount. The 13.3B figure is unconfirmed and likely inflated; however, the event is directionally correct. Flagging as VERIFIED with caveat on the specific figure.

title: Former Orbán ally Péter Magyar launches large-scale opposition movement
note: Magyar emerged February 2024 after Novák pardon scandal; TISZA ~30% in June 2024 EP election vs FIDESZ 44% confirmed.
